column2: Build a Library

Verena gave mankind the written word, and the Order of Mysteries keeps what was written. A brother of the Order without a library of his own is a scholar without a desk, and you must build one in which the lost lore you recover can be studied, copied and kept.
To complete this mission, take the decision §Y'Build a Library'§! in the Intrigue menu and see the building through to the end.
Find an Apprentice

Every Lorekeeper worth the name takes on an apprentice. Somebody must copy the crumbling scrolls, keep the catalogue in order and carry the lantern down into the ruins, and what [Root.GetTitle] has the time to do all that alone?
§Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! must name an apprentice through the §YMinor Titles§! screen, or keep [Root.GetHerHis] eyes open for a promising pupil, to complete this mission.
Recover a Lost Text

Your colleague [FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName] has come upon a letter naming the hiding places of several lost writings. A bargain has been struck: [FromFrom.GetFirstName] brings the letter and the learning, you pay for the expedition, and the Order of Mysteries shall have the find for its Mysterious Volumes.
If §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! sets out on one of the expeditions §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! suggests and finds the lost text, the mission is completed.
Raid the Hoard of [FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName]

[FromFrom.GetSocietyRank] [FromFrom.GetFirstName] hoards books like a Scrollbearer, locking away what Verena gave to all. The Goddess teaches that knowledge belongs to everyone, and in that spirit you and a colleague have agreed to break into [FromFrom.GetFirstName]'s library, carry off what [FromFrom.GetSheHe] will not share and leave [FromFrom.GetHerHis] scriptorium in no state to hoard any more. Not a single page will burn, of course. You are not Witch Hunters.
Your colleague will bring you to the library of §Y[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]§!. If you take or wreck something and get away unseen, the mission is completed.
Tablet of Lybaras

A tablet of green stone from the sealed archives of Lybaras, the city of scholars of old Nehekhara, where the priest kings made inventors and stargazers of their subjects. Its glyphs record the laws by which one substance becomes another and the courses of the stars above the desert. Every scholar who has read a line of it calls it the greatest find of the Order of Mysteries, and every Witch Hunter calls it something else.
whether it's true that I keep a tablet from the tombs of Lybaras at home or not

A true library takes years and gold to assemble, and without one I shall never see further than the next village. The Lorekeepers say that Verena lifted mankind from barbarism with the gift of writing. It is time I gave those writings a proper home.
For knowledge!
On second thought, there are more pressing matters.

Where shall the library stand? What I mean to keep there will frighten the ignorant, tempt my brothers and sisters of the Order and, sooner or later, draw a Witch Hunter to my door. Many a Lorekeeper hides the books deep within the castle walls, but a hall open to every honest reader is what the Goddess truly asks of us.
Deep within the walls of [Root.Capital.Capital.GetName], where no zealot will find it.
The library must fit into your castle. Your books will be safe, but your household will live beside them.
In a hall open to every scholar, as Verena wills.
Nothing will stand in the way of a fine library, but anyone may walk in.
In a guarded house on an island, where only boats can reach it.
In a guarded house far out in the country.
Far from prying eyes the library can be as large as it needs to be, and a thief will have to find it first.

The master builder has unrolled his plans across my table. A reading room with a few shelves would serve. So would a scriptorium with copying desks, or a hall of learning with a reading gallery under a painted ceiling of owls. And then there is the drawing he keeps at the bottom of the pile, the one modelled on the Grand Temple of Verena at Nuln.
A reading room will do.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a small but useful library.
A scriptorium, with desks for copyists.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a library where books can be copied as well as read.
A hall of learning, worthy of the Order.
[Root.GetFullName] will aim for a great library with reading rooms, a scriptorium and an archive.
Something to make the Lorekeepers of Nuln weep with envy.
[Root.GetFullName] will build a library to rival the Grand Temple of Nuln, with every gallery, vault and desk the plans can hold.

A library is only as good as its copyists. The scribes of the town write a fair hand for contracts and tavern signs, but the brothers of the Temple of Clio the Scrivener at Carroburg copy a crumbling scroll so faithfully that the copy outlives the original by a thousand years. They do not come cheap.
The town scribes will learn.
Send for the scriveners of Carroburg.

Every Verenan remembers the sack of Wolfenburg, when the Order wept more for the burning books than for the dead. Tallow candles are cheap, and so are buckets of sand. Stone vaults and shuttered lanterns of Nuln brass are not.
Candles and sand. We shall be careful.
No flame shall touch these shelves unshuttered.

Half the old books I mean to keep are falling apart in my hands. The local tanner offers calfskin for new bindings, while the binders of Marienburg work in vellum and boards that keep out damp, worm and the careless thumb alike, for a merchant's price.
The tanner's calfskin will hold.
Only Marienburg bindings for my books.

And then the books themselves, the heart of every library and, to the Cult of Verena, holy every one of them. I have a fair number already. A fair number is not a library. The booksellers of Altdorf have lists, the University of Nuln sells its spare copies, and the printers have begun to flood the Empire with cheap books, to the horror of the followers of Scripsisti.
The books I have will be quite enough for now.
Buy every book worth the reading!
[Root.GetFullName] will spare [Root.GetHerHis] purse, and the library will be the poorer for it.
[Root.GetFullName] will pay for the best, and the library will be the better for it.

It is hardly the Grand Temple of Nuln, and a visiting Lorekeeper would call it a cupboard with ambitions, but it is mine. The shelves stand, the desk is lit and the catalogue fits on a single page. The Owl will show me the way from here.

The work is done. My library may not compare to the great libraries of Altdorf and Nuln, but its shelves are full, its copyists busy and its catalogue in good order. It will serve me well in the search for what the world has forgotten.

The library is finished, and it is a fine one. Scholars write to ask whether they may read in it, and a passing Knight of the Scroll stood in the doorway for some time before he remembered to take off his helmet. Will it bring me the wisdom I seek? Only Verena knows.
Time to open the books...
Let the reading begin!
The Ambition of a [Root.GetTitle]
The House of Learning

After months of hard work and a small fortune in gold, the library of [Root.GetFullName] is the envy of every Lorekeeper who hears of it. Its galleries hold the learning of half the Old World, its scriptorium copies a dozen books a season and its archive keeps writings that even the Order of Mysteries thought lost. It stands as a monument to the [Root.GetTitle]'s ambition.

No expense was spared. Under the eye of [Root.GetFullName] a house of learning has risen that is spoken of in Altdorf, Marienburg and Nuln alike. The owls carved over the gate keep watch over vaults of stone, a scriptorium of forty desks and a reading hall where the [Root.GetTitle]'s own scales of Verena hang above the catalogue.\n\nHigh Priestess van der Perssen herself has written to ask when she may come to debate on its steps. It wants only its master to begin.
Follow the Owl!
Let the debating begin!

The whole castle woke to shouting in the night. A lamp left burning in the reading room has fallen into a heap of loose pages, and by the time the bucket chain reached it the new shelves were ablaze. We saved most of the books, Verena be praised, but not everyone came out unhurt.
Better skin than books, alas.
We must guard against fire properly this time...
[Root.GetFullName] will spend gold on stone vaults and shuttered lanterns, so the library suffers less.

A preacher of Sigmar has been haranguing the market square for three days. 'Heretics! Every temple of Verena harbours forbidden writings, and now the [Root.GetTitle] is building another nest for them!' This morning a small mob gathered at the gate demanding to know which books I keep, and whether any of them have been written by daemons.
Show them the shelves. Let them see there is nothing to fear.
[Root.GetFullName] will change [Root.GetHerHis] plans to calm the townsfolk rather than to build the best library.
Since when does the [Root.GetTitle] answer to a rabble?

Disaster! A sweet, rotten smell from the cellar led my servants to the crates of books I bought this spring. Damp has crept into the bindings, black mould blooms across the pages and the bookworms have eaten their way through a whole treatise on canon law. So much for leaving them there until the shelves were ready.
Save what can be saved.
Build a dry store for them, at once!

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

It has come to my attention that you still have no library worth the name! I cannot imagine how you hope to recover the lost lore of Verena without proper shelves, copyists and an archive. My own library has become a second home to me, and to half the scholars of the province. You would do well to follow my example, or your work will be forgotten before the ink is dry.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

Master, forgive my boldness, but I fear we are both held back for want of a proper library. Every book we recover ends up in a chest under my bed, and the mice have already eaten a chapter of the Mysterious Volumes. If we are to keep what Verena gave us, we need shelves, desks and a dry vault. Build a library, Master, I beg you.

Your devoted apprentice,
[From.GetFirstName]

With a library of my own I can take on mysteries I would not have dared before. How I ever worked from a chest of books and a kitchen table I shall never understand. The lost lore of Verena is within my reach.

My new library is the envy of my brothers and sisters of the Order. Even Manfred Archibald, who founded the Order of Mysteries and has seen the archives of every great temple in the Empire, would be hard pressed to find fault with it.
My work has only begun.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

I must say, dear colleague, I do not know how you manage without an apprentice! Mine copies a page faster than any scrivener of Clio, carries the lantern into the foulest crypt without a word of complaint and has never once smelled of ale. Take my advice and find one of your own.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

For months the thought of an apprentice has followed me about the castle. None of my councillors would do, and I dare not ask the priests of the town. But one of my servants has caught my eye. [From.GetFirstName] reads every scrap of paper [From.GetSheHe] dusts, and this morning I found [From.GetHerHim] correcting the Classical in one of my own notes.
[From.GetSheHeCap] knows how to listen, at the very least.
Surely I can find someone worthier than a servant!
You keep looking for an apprentice.

I have a good feeling about this! With [From.GetFirstName] as my apprentice there is no end to what we may recover. Lost tombs, forgotten archives, perhaps even a page or two that never made it into the Mysterious Volumes.
Bright times are ahead.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My [Root.GetSisterBrother], I have a proposal that may interest you. Not long ago an old letter came into my hands, written by a brother of the Order of Mysteries who died before he could follow it up. It names the hiding places of several lost writings. You have the purse and I have the letter. Shall we search for them together, in the true spirit of the Order?

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

The letter names three lost texts. A tome among the stock of an antiquarian in [Root.Capital.GetName], a scroll walled up in a temple at [temple_site.GetName], and a tablet in the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName] in [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. The further we go, the older the find and the greater its secrets. The choice is yours.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

I bring the best of news! Since I last wrote, I have bought from a Tilean tomb robber a map that leads to a sealed archive of Lybaras, the city of scholars of old Nehekhara, where the priest kings kept their inventors and stargazers. If the map is true, the archive holds the Tablet of Lybaras itself. I will not hide the danger. Brother Oliver's expedition into the Land of the Dead went looking for the Book of Dust, and he alone came back. The other places remain, the tome in [Root.Capital.GetName], the scroll in [temple_site.GetName] and the tablet in [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName], but I would argue that a chance like this comes once in a lifetime.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
To Lybaras, and may the dead stay asleep.
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out across the Great Desert for the sealed archive of Lybaras. This chance will not come again in your lifetime.\n
Let us travel to the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName].
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out for [ruin_site.GetName], hoping to find the tablet in the ruins there.\n
a successful search.\n
The scroll in [temple_site.GetName] seems the wisest choice.
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! set out for [temple_site.GetName], hoping to find the scroll in a temple there.\n
I have little to spare... Surely the antiquarian will do?
You and §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! go through the stock of an antiquarian in search of the old tome.\n
The Tablet of Lybaras

When we found the door to the archive, carved with the scales and stars of Lybaras, we could hardly believe our eyes. [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I had nearly given up. We had seen the bone-white sentinels pacing the dunes at dusk and heard something vast moving beneath the sand, and that day was to be the last of our search. Surely only the Goddess could have led us there! My hands shook as I helped the servants heave the last stone aside.\n\nLantern held high, my colleague and I went in first. The light fell on jars of sealed scrolls, star charts painted across the walls and the bronze gears of some engine of the old priest kings. And something deep within the chamber gave the light back, something vividly green... [From.GetFirstName]'s breath came quick and shallow. 'It... it cannot be!'
The learning of Lybaras returns to the world. Praise Verena!

Our journey into foreign lands met with no small amount of trouble, but at last we reached the ruins of [ruin_site.GetName] safely. After a fortnight of digging the servants laid bare the mouth of a buried chamber. [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went in side by side, and the lantern showed us a tablet set into the far wall, its glyphs untouched by a thousand years.
Are those glyphs Nehekharan, or older still?

A generous gift to the temple of [temple_site.GetName] persuaded its priest to open the inner chambers to us. We searched every niche and crypt for the hiding place of the scroll, and on the fifth day a servant called us to a loose stone behind the altar...
We found it, [From.GetFirstName]!

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went through every shelf and chest of the dusty little shop. For days on end we did nothing but breathe dust and leaf through almanacs, sermons and bad poetry. So you may imagine my surprise when, on the fourth day, an owl looked up at me from the spine of a battered old book.
I think this is it, [From.GetFirstName]!

My doubts began soon after we left the last oasis, but [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] swore we had only misread the map. After every empty valley [From.GetSheHe] had a new idea, and after every night we lost more servants to the things that walk the dunes. When at last we fled north with half the camels and none of the gold, a suspicion crept over me... What if the map was forged, and [From.GetFirstName] knew it all along? Was the whole expedition a plot to ruin me?

Our journey into foreign lands met with every trouble the road can offer, from foul weather to lame horses, but our guide was the end of it. When that scoundrel ran off with the last of our gold, we found that we were not even in the right part of [ruin_site.Holder.TopLiege.PrimaryTitle.GetName]!

A generous gift to the temple of [temple_site.GetName] persuaded its priest to open the inner chambers to us. We searched every niche and crypt for the hiding place of the scroll, and after a week we had found nothing more interesting than a bundle of rather lewd letters. We had to admit defeat.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and I went through every shelf and chest of the dusty little shop. For days on end we did nothing but breathe dust and leaf through almanacs, sermons and bad poetry. After a week we had to admit defeat. There was nothing of worth in that place.

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] is a pompous, featherbrained Scrollbearer. You know it to be true, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]! [infiltration_target.GetSheHeCap] buys up every book in the province and lets no one read them, not even the Order. It is time someone set them free. Let us break into [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library, carry off what [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] hoards and leave [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] scriptorium in no state to hoard any more!

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My friend, we have a common foe. You know of whom I speak, that miser [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName]! A member of our Order who locks away the gifts of Verena like a dragon on its gold. It makes me sick! Let us break into [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library and share with the world what [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] will not.

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

To [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] sits on the finest hoard of books and curiosities in the province and has not lent out so much as an almanac in ten years. The Scrollbearers would be proud. What do you say, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]? Shall we pay [infiltration_target.GetHerHim] a visit by night and claim what should belong to all?

May the Owl watch over you.
[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]

Most esteemed [Root.GetSocietyRank] [Root.GetFirstName],

My spies have not yet found where [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] keeps [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library. Do not worry, my friend, they have several promising leads. A cart of books bought in Altdorf must go somewhere. We need only be patient.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName]
I shall be ready to leave at a moment's notice.
As soon as the spies of §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! have found the library, you will set out.\n

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] must be as fearful as [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] is greedy, for [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library is a walled house far from any road. As we creep closer under cover of night, [From.GetFirstName] whispers to me about the guards. A Knight of the Scroll, by the look of the armour, and two hired swords. We will only get one chance at this.

[infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] has hidden [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] library deep beneath [infiltration_target.Capital.GetName]. Thanks to [From.GetFirstName]'s spies we have come this far unseen, but the last door is guarded, and the guards look awake.

'It was not hard to find [infiltration_target.GetFirstName]'s library,' [From.GetFirstName] tells me as we slip into the [infiltration_target.Capital.GetHolding]. 'Old [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] cannot keep a secret to save [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] life, but [infiltration_target.GetSheHe] does know how to hire good guards.' [From.GetSheHeCap] points down the corridor, at the problem ahead.
I have a way with people, and a heavy purse.
You try to bribe the guards.\n
I brewed a sleeping draught for this very moment.
You try to drug the guards with a draught of your own making.\n
a successful scheme.
a failed scheme, and discovery.
You draw them off, I will slip inside.
§Y[infiltration_companion.GetTitledFirstName]§! tries to lure the guards away. You will have to do the work inside alone, so you can do less harm.\n
On second thought, this is madness...
You slip away and go home to your [Root.Capital.GetHolding].\n

As we step out of the shadows the guards draw their swords, but their faces change when I lift the heavy purse from my belt. After a few quiet words and the clink of coin, [infiltration_companion.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] and I pass through the heavy door into a hall of shelves that reaches up into darkness. 'Well, my [Root.GetSisterBrother]?' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] whispers. 'How shall we go about it?'

By some miracle, [infiltration_companion.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] manages to empty the little vial into the jug before it is carried to the guards. Within a quarter of an hour they are snoring softly. 'We must hurry, the draught will not last forever,' I whisper as we step over them. Inside, the shelves reach up into darkness. 'Well?' [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] asks. 'How shall we go about it?'
You wreck the scriptorium, I will find the books.
You split up to cover more ground. Quicker, but riskier.\n
Leave the scriptorium to me. Take whatever you can carry.
Help me find where [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] keeps [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] best books.
You stay together. Safer, but you can do less.\n
Let us leave this place in no state to hoard ever again!

Everything went so well at first. [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] emptied the vial into the jug without anyone noticing. That was half an hour ago. The guards show no sign of drowsiness, one of them is singing, and our time is running out. I whisper my apologies as we creep away, but [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] does not answer.
That recipe has never failed me before, I swear...

I had my doubts, but I must admit I am impressed! [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] drew the guards off by crying fire in the stable yard, and they ran out with their buckets as one man. Every Verenan knows that cry would clear any library in the Empire. I do not know how long I have. What now?
Find the rarest books and the hidden cabinet!
Wreck the scriptorium, scatter the catalogue!

I have seen many foolish things in my day, but [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName]'s distraction may take the prize. [infiltration_companion.GetSheHeCap] began to rattle a chain against the wall and wail like a ghost of the library! When the guards' footsteps came closer I seized [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the sleeve and ran. 'A ghost? Really? Nobody with any sense would fall for that!'
There will be no second attempt tonight. Nor for a long, long time.

I am about to sweep the copying desks clear when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and find myself face to face with the guards. Our eyes meet for a moment before I drop the inkpot and run, but it is no use. Even half-drugged they are faster than me.

I am about to sweep the copying desks clear when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and look straight into the panicked eyes of [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName], and only then do I see the guards holding [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the arms. 'Run!' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] cries, but it is too late.

My arms are full of books from the hidden cabinet when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and find myself face to face with the guards. Our eyes meet for a moment before I drop the books and run, but it is no use. Even half-drugged they are faster than me.

My arms are full of books from the hidden cabinet when the door opens behind me. I whirl around and look straight into the panicked eyes of [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName], and only then do I see the guards holding [infiltration_companion.GetHerHim] by the arms. 'Run!' [infiltration_companion.GetSheHe] cries, but it is too late.
Unhand me! I am a colleague of your [infiltration_target.GetMasterMistress]!

It seems my guards have caught a pair of rats among the shelves! [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] and [From.GetHerHis] accomplice [infiltration_companion.GetFirstName] tried to break into my library and help themselves to my books. Brothers of the Order, if you please! Such an insult cannot go unanswered...
Perhaps [From.GetFirstName] will trade a few secrets for [From.GetHerHis] freedom.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! refuses to share [From.GetHerHis] secrets and stays in the cell.\n
Leave them in the dungeon. I will deal with them later...

I had come to the point of begging for water when the guards dragged me out of the cell. I must have fainted, for the next thing I see is the scornful face of [From.GetFirstName]. 'Well, well. A thief who calls [Root.GetHerselfHimself] a brother of the Order! Verena is the goddess of justice too, you know.' After a few more insults, [From.GetSheHe] offers me my freedom in exchange for the secrets of my own library.
Give me water, and I will tell you whatever you wish.
You will never be worthy of my secrets!
You stay in the cell.\n

I barely knew [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] when they dragged [From.GetHerHim] before me. A few days in the dungeon will do that. So eager was [From.GetSheHe] for freedom that I could have asked for [From.GetHerHis] firstborn. Instead [From.GetFirstName] filled notebook after notebook with everything [From.GetSheHe] knows, under my stern gaze and the eye of the Owl.
This will make for interesting reading.

I barely knew [From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetFirstName] when they dragged [From.GetHerHim] before me. A few days in the dungeon will do that. It seems [From.GetSheHe] has grown fond of [From.GetHerHis] cell, however, for my generous offer earned me nothing but insults and curses.
Enjoy your cell, [From.GetFirstName].

I had come to the point of begging for water when the guards dragged me out of the cell. I must have fainted, for the next thing I see is the scornful face of [From.GetFirstName]. 'Well, well. A thief who calls [Root.GetHerselfHimself] a brother of the Order! I only wanted a look at you before they throw away the key...'
Mercy, mercy! Not back in there!

Who would have thought the library of [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] held such a treasure? Behind a false shelf I find a locked cabinet, and in it, wrapped in silk like a holy relic, the greatest book in the whole hoard. Beside it lie a purse of crowns and a few curiosities that will fetch good coin in the quieter streets of [Root.Capital.GetName].

My search has been well worth the risk. [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName]'s cabinet of rare substances is a fine sight, and a little purse of crowns was tucked behind the catalogue. My share of the spoils will be a fine addition to my own library.

For all [infiltration_target.GetHerHis] boasting I expected more. Or perhaps [infiltration_target.GetSocietyRank] [infiltration_target.GetFirstName] hides the good books better than I thought. Either way I find nothing of great worth, only a purse of crowns in the desk.
Knowledge belongs to all! Well, to me, for now.
A fine haul. Verena would approve. Probably.
It is better than nothing, I suppose.
You take the finest book of the hoard. It will be added to your treasury.\n
You take a rare substance from the cabinet. It will be added to your treasury.\n

If I ever find the thief who broke into my library, I will see [From.GetHerHim] hanged! The cabinet behind the false shelf stands empty, my rarest substances are gone and so is the greatest book I own. My finest knowledge, my deepest secrets! May Verena's scales find the thief wanting!

If I ever find the thief who broke into my library, I will see [From.GetHerHim] hanged! The cabinet of rare substances has been plundered, and the purse behind the catalogue is gone. No common burglar knew where to look. It must have been a brother of the Order!

I must see to the guards of my library. Last night some wretch slipped past them, but by Verena's grace nothing of real worth was taken. Either the thief had no idea what my books are worth, or [From.GetSheHe] was too dull to find them. The purse in my desk is gone, though.

No Verenan would burn a book, not even this one. But a library is more than its books. I smash the copying desks, pour the inks over the half-finished copies, break the reading lenses and, last of all, tear the catalogue to pieces and scatter it through the galleries.
